# Procedures and Outputs

This is the “language basics” chapter: how Tactus procedures take inputs, return typed outputs, and fail fast when inputs don’t match what you expect.

## This Chapter Will Cover

- The two common styles you’ll see in this book:
  - Script-style procedures with top-level `input { ... }` / `output { ... }`
  - `Procedure { ... }` blocks (when you want explicit procedure configuration)
- Defining inputs: required fields, defaults, and descriptions (`field.string`, `field.number`, `field.boolean`, etc.)
- Defining outputs: structured results, validation, and “return tables”
- Parameters vs inputs (`--param key=value` vs `input { ... }`)
- Practical error handling patterns (use `assert(...)` / `error(...)` to fail loudly)

## How It Connects to the Running Example

We’ll revisit the meeting-recap workflow from Part II and give it a clean, typed contract (inputs like “raw notes” and “recipient”, outputs like “draft subject/body”, and later “message_id”).
